subject.title: 2026.7.2-beta.1 startup migration rejects Memory Core FTS triggers created by the same build

question: Should compact validation explicitly admit registered extension-owned SQLite objects, or should Memory Core temporarily remove and restore only its canonical triggers around the assertion?
rationale: Both approaches can resolve the immediate failure, but the permanent ownership boundary affects future plugins and potentially the public SQLite runtime contract.

options.title: Registry-aware validation
options.body: Teach the validator to recognize narrowly registered extension-owned objects and test both core-only and Memory Core schemas.

options.title: Scoped trigger bracketing
options.body: Keep the validator core-only and expose a supported path for Memory Core to remove and restore its three canonical triggers in a guaranteed cleanup block.

recommendation.title: Registry-aware validation
recommendation.body: Teach the validator to recognize narrowly registered extension-owned objects and test both core-only and Memory Core schemas.

likelyOwner.reason: The regression is tied to the beta integration window and needs routing across release, core SQLite, and bundled Memory Core ownership.
